summary:
# NOTES: Two books (BOOK 1 = Starvel Hollow; BOOK 2 = Adventures of Bindle)

## BOOK 1 of 2: The Starvel Hollow Tragedy (Freeman Wills Crofts; Inspector French)

**Characters:** Ruth Averill (20, niece, orphan, dark, small, dependent); Simon Averill (miser, invalid, ~elderly, safe full of notes/gold, Starvel house, dies in fire); John Roper (manservant, Scots from Fife, squint, sly, drunk allegedly; forger, blackmailer, murderer); Flora (Mrs.) Roper (née Macfarlane, sharp-tongued, killed); Markham Giles (entomologist, ex-soldier, gassed/wounded, heart; cottage half mile from Starvel; killed by cocaine injection, buried in coffin under name of Roper's victim); Pierce Whymper (junior architect, Leeds firm Nixon & Arbuthnot, clerk of works at Thirsby church, son of Stephen Whymper surgeon; lover of Ruth; passed £20 notes); Mr. Oxley (solicitor, jovial, wife Mrs. Oxley); Mr. Tarkington (bank manager, Thirsby, thin hawk-like; suspected fireproof safe); Bloxham (bank clerk, sardonic face); Sergeant Kent (Thirsby police, bumptious); Dr. Emerson (old doctor, certified Giles' death); Dr. Herbert Philpot (Thirsby doctor, gambler, faked influenza; murderer of wife Edna and of Roper, Giles, Averill); Dr. Lonsdale (coroner); Chief Constable Valentine (Leeds); Inspector Joseph French (Scotland Yard CID); Chief Inspector Mitchell; Inspector Willis; Inspector Tanner; Sergeant Elliott; Sergeant Carter; Constable Sheldrake; Judith Carr (barmaid, Thirsdale Arms); George Mellowes (farmer, drove Roper home drunk); Mr. Pullar (shoe shop, identified heel); Mrs. Palmer-Gore (York, sent invitation); Colonel Followes (magistrate); Dr. Lingard (Hellifield police surgeon); Mr. Dashwood & Mr. Munce (stockbrokers, Gracechurch St.); Mr. Stanley (salesman); Mr. Russell; Mr. Alderdice (jeweller); Philpot's Glasgow landlady Mrs. MacIntosh, 47 Kilgore St.; Mr. Gunny (Chief Inspector, Bindle book only—ignore).

**Places:** Starvel (old house in circular Hollow on Yorkshire moor, near Thirsby; Starvel Hollow); Thirsby (small town; Thirsdale Arms hotel; St. ... church; Stanhope Terrace); Oakdene, Ashton Drive, York; Braeside, Kintilloch, Fife (Ransome Institute, mental hospital); Talloires/Annecy (Savoy; Hotel Splendide); Cable Street/Tower Bridge (rings); Peveril Hotel, Russell Sq; Waverley Station, Edinburgh; Glasgow (Kilgore St.); Peebles (Roper's mother).

**Timeline (key events):**
- 10 Sept 1921? (text: Sept, Roper's note dated Sept 10); Ruth sent to York by note from "Helen Palmer-Gore" with £10 from uncle, via Roper. Ruth leaves Tues; Starvel burned night of Wed 15 Sept (baker sees smoke Thu morning).
- Giles dies Tues; Mrs Roper said she visited; Giles' body found by Roper; funeral Friday.
- Inquest: three bodies (Averill, Ropers) verdict accidental; Roper said drunk (Mellowes, Judith Carr).
- Mid-Oct: Tarkington reports £20 note (from £320 sent to Starvel) paid in London; Oxley; Chief Constable Valentine called.
- French: Starvel safe ash = newspapers (Leeds Mercury 13–15 Sept); Carter & Stephenson safe maker.
- Whymper's £20 notes (24 found, £480); Cook's; Whymper trip to Talloires (Prosper Giraud, Mme Madeleine Blancquart — fictitious story by Roper).
- Confession forged by Philpot (Kintilloch, wife Edna killed 15 May 1921 by cricket bat after cord trip); Roper blackmail; Mrs. Philpot's death.
- Exhumation of Giles coffin (empty of body, half-full earth); yellow clay in shed; body found buried on moor near Starvel; Dr. Lingard PM: cocaine injection.
- Roper's disguise: wedding rings thrown from Tower Bridge by lightermen Gray & Fuller (Chief Insp. Mitchell's theory); rings bought in London by "dark moustache, tinted glasses" man paying £20 notes; Dashwood & Munce; trap at Waverley Station, Edinburgh, Tue; Philpot helps identify; Philpot pulled Mills bomb; caught; Tanner acts as Munce.
- Conclusion: Philpot confessed; £36,562 recovered in steel cashbox at Glasgow; Ruth and Whymper marry; Philpot hanged.

**Key facts:** Averill safe: 1952 sovereigns; £30–40k notes; £20 notes numbered list (193 notes, 11 consignments). Tarkington's clerk Bloxham. Cook's office; Thirsby pub "Thirsdale Arms" landlord gossip. Roper's cut thumb (right thumb). Roper's description: 34, 5ft 9, squint, thick dark hair, moustache disguise. Ruth's father Theodore Averill (wine merchant, Bayonne), mother Anne de Condillac, married 1905, Ruth born 1906 at Biarritz.

## BOOK 2 of 2: Adventures of Bindle (Herbert George Jenkins)

**Characters:** Joseph "Joe" Bindle (furniture remover, special constable, Fulham; cricket cap, pipe, "Cheer-o"; wife Mrs. Lizzie Bindle, Christian, strict, bangs pans, dislikes swearing); Mr. Alfred "Alf" Hearty (greengrocer, brother-in-law of Bindle; pompous, wheezy; shops in Putney/Fulham/Wandsworth; hymns; wife Martha Hearty, wheezes, laughs); Millie (Millicent) Hearty (niece, sweetheart Charlie Dixon, sergeant 110th London Regiment; marries him); Mr. Josiah Gupperduck (lodger, temperance, accordion, lecturer; beaten at peace meeting in Hyde Park); Rev. Andrew MacFie (Scotch minister, Alton Road Chapel; courts Millie; secret wife "Cissie"?—woman claiming to be his wife at conversazione); Rev. James Sopley (retiring minister); Lady Knob-Kerrick (Barton Bridge/The Poplars, Putney Hill; haughty); Miss Strint (companion); Mr. Wilton (butler); John (footman); Mrs. Marlings (housekeeper); Ginger (friend, spits, "I don't 'old wiv"; twins); Wilkes (coughs); Huggles (driver); Tippitt (weedy youth, cigarette); Spotty; Scratcher (waiter friend, Napolini's); Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino (Italian waiter); Herr/Mr. James Smith (chief superintendent, Napolini's); Dick Little (doctor, Chelsea) and brother Tom; Guggers (Captain, Gordons, gug-gug stammer); "Nancy" Dane (Pierrot); Chief-Inspector Gunny; Mrs. Sedge (Charlie Hart's mother-in-law, gin); Charlie Hart (Bindle's friend, porter Fulham Sq. Mansions); Miss Cissie Boye (actress, Flat Six); Mr. Jabez Stiffson (flat six; wife Mrs. Stiffson); Oscar (canary); Mr. Llewellyn John (Prime Minister, 110 Downing St.); Mr. Pain & Mrs. Pain, Mr. & Mrs. Withers, Mr. & Mrs. Gash, Miss Torkington, Mr. Tuddenham & Mr. Muskett, Mr. Dixon (Charlie's uncle), Mrs. Dixon; Mr. Smith (potato cellar); Billy Nips (errand boy); Mrs. Rogers (neighbour); Horace Gaze (anecdote); Alice (Heartys' maid); Ruddy Bill; Alf Gorley; Pincher Nobbs.

**Chapters (summary):**
1. The Coming of the Lodger: Mrs. Bindle answers ad in *Gospel Sentinel* "Lonely"; Mr. Gupperduck moves in (accordion; "Pleasant for the ducks"); Bindle teases.
2. A Downing Street Sensation: Bindle, with Tippitt, delivers a pantechnicon of Black-and-White suffragette raiders (Votes for Women) hidden inside, lamp-blacked by Bindle via watering can and pea-puffer; inspector arrests/disperses; Chief-Inspector Gunny praises him.
3. The Air-Raid: Gupperduck and Hearty hide in potato cellar; Bindle drops scales; Mrs. Bindle faints; Millie's loyalty.
4. Duplication of Mr. Hearty: six lookalike "Hearty" alibis; Mr. Hearty's third shop; advertised by Bindle with Dick Little/Guggers scheme.
5. Gathering of the Bands: Hearty's shop advertised by donkeys/camel with boards, bands (Salvation-style) invade; police.
6. Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap: beaten at Peace meeting, Hyde Park; Bindle refuses to house him.
7. Courting of Rev. Andrew MacFie: MacFie courts Millie; Bindle's Uriah/David jibe.
8. Chapel Conversazione: glee party; Lady Knob-Kerrick; MacFie's secret wife; woman in toque; whistle; "Nancy" Dane disguise.
9. Letting of Number Six: Bindle as temporary porter Fulham Square Mansions; Miss Cissie Boye and Mr. Stiffson.
10. Downfall of Mr. Jabez Stiffson: porridge bowl; Mrs. Stiffson; lift stuck.
11. Camouflaging of Mr. Gupperduck: Ginger; Gupperduck's bruises.
12. Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino: Bindle waiter at Napolini's; chaos; Tolmenicino arrested as spy.
13. Return of Charlie Dixon: Millie and Charlie marry proposal; Bindle persuades.
14. Mr. Hearty Yields: Bindle blackmails Hearty over "Mrs. ..." (fake story); consents.
15. A Billeting Adventure: Harridge's pantechnicon of 16 bedsteads sent to Lady Knob-Kerrick's drawing-room; sergeant and soldiers; Ginger's herring.
16. Millie's Wedding: Charlie and Millie married; Mr. Sopley officiates; Bindle's speech; Mrs. Dixon's remark; Bindle and Mr. Dixon leave.

**Bindle quotes:** "Lodgers ain't to be trusted"; "Gawd made me, an' Gawd made 'Earty"; "Are we downhearted? Noooo!"
